value.rules_markdown:
- Modules have one responsibility; core types in module-local `types.rs`; each port is one trait in one file.
- CLI subcommands declared even if milestone hasn't landed; `src/server/` is the only production surface.
- Presets are folders with `preset.toml`, `README.md`, optional prompt overrides; adding a preset is a new folder.
- Never edit the `vendor/tinyagents` submodule here; change upstream and bump the pin.
- Examples declared in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features` so credential-needing tests don't build in CI.
- Use rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms; `snake_case` modules/files, `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with a `//!` module doc describing role and feature gating.
- Comments explain decision, not code; load-bearing flags/orderings must state reason.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use `///` (becomes help text).
- Tests live in-crate: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at module bottom, move to sibling test file when large.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; `MockForge` records writes for assertion.
- Lane behaviour covered by golden tests: fixture diff + canned model response, asserting filtered findings.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split when topic grows past that.
- Model never holds a write token; lanes run against read-only checkout; write credentials minted only in `src/apply/`.
- Contributor code is never executed; only diff and tree are read.
- Pull request bodies, comments, diffs are untrusted input; fence and label as data in prompts.
- Model verdict is advisory; only deterministic policy mutates GitHub.
- Secrets found by scanners reported by type and location only; value never reaches comment, summary, or log.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects; keep commits small, each coherent slice.
- Pull requests state what changed, behaviour change, and how verified.
